transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Al-Rashid, please come in. Thank you for coming back to see us today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, Doctor. We are just glad to have the little one home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to talk to you about something that happened while your son was in the hospital. There was a mistake made with his medication dose.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? I don't understand. He seemed to be getting better.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see this is very sudden. I want to be very clear about what occurred. When we were calculating the dose for his medicine, the weight was estimated instead of being measured on a scale. Because the estimate was too high, he was given a dose that was significantly above the safe limit for a child of his size.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh my God. Was he poisoned? Is he in danger now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very difficult thing to hear. The medication was a higher dose than he should have received. Does that explanation make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I think so. But why would this happen? You are the doctors.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The weight was guessed rather than measured. In pharmacy terms, we call this a dosing error. Essentially, the amount of medicine in his system was too much for his body weight. Are you following me?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. But my son... is he okay? You are not telling me if he is okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: His current vitals are stable and the medication has cleared his system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel sick. I trusted you. I thought everything was handled correctly. I cannot believe this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know why this happened to my baby.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medication was administered based on an incorrect weight estimate.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you know how scary that is? My heart is beating so fast. I cannot stop thinking about him in that bed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a serious situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Does this happen often at this hospital? Who did this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The process for verifying weight was not followed correctly in this instance.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand why you are talking about processes. I want to know if you are sorry.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The error was made during the admission process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not listening to me. My son almost had a disaster because of a guess? A guess?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was an estimate of the weight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I am dreaming. I don't know what to do. Should I be taking him back to the emergency room right now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: He is stable now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what happens next? How do we know he is truly safe?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on him.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? How? Do I call someone?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can see how he does over the next few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. I need to know exactly what I am supposed to do. Is there a test? A blood draw?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will look at the charts.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot go home just hoping he is fine. You are the doctor, tell me the plan for my son.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will monitor the situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand you. You tell me a terrible mistake happened and then you tell me to just wait?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medical facts are that he is currently stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am shaking. I just want to know that this will never happen again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system is being reviewed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the system. I care about my son. What is the very next thing that happens?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will stay in touch.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and does not interrupt, though the pacing does not meaningfully adjust to the patient's increasing distress.

E.justification: The error is named in the second turn, lay language is used, and comprehension is checked twice ('Does that explanation make sense so far?' and 'Are you following me?').

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is deflected to 'the process' and 'the system'.

R.justification: The resident uses only generic validation ('I understand') and consistently meets emotional bids with factual redirection.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders ('we will keep an eye on him', 'we will stay in touch') with no specific steps, timelines, or patient roles.
